builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MemoryTax: The Bitter Lesson of Agent Memory
summary: It replaces pre-question memory extraction systems such as Mem0 and Zep, and partly full-context prompting, by keeping the raw conversation history and letting a capable model search it with agent tools at query time. It eliminates the memory-writing pipeline and its build cost, but shifts spend to per-query tool-using rollouts whose cost and latency depend on the model and retrieval loop. It can fail because the advantage rests on a strong reader model and on agent-readable artifacts such as photo captions, and with weaker models designed memory still wins; the evidence base is one conversation with one run per cell.
rationale: The finding that strong models can replace curated memory with self-directed search is directly actionable on API budgets, but a single-conversation, single-run study requires workload-specific validation before production adoption.
technique: Agent-side search over raw history instead of designed memory

claims.statement: It replaces pre-question memory extraction systems such as Mem0 and Zep, and partly full-context prompting, by keeping the raw conversation history and letting a capable model search it with agent tools at query time. It eliminates the memory-writing pipeline and its build cost, but shifts spend to per-query tool-using rollouts whose cost and latency depend on the model and retrieval loop. It can fail because the advantage rests on a strong reader model and on agent-readable artifacts such as photo captions, and with weaker models designed memory still wins; the evidence base is one conversation with one run per cell.
With Claude Opus 5.5, the Pi coding agent reaches 99% accuracy for less than half the cost of a full-context rollout; Mem0's memory build alone costs more than an entire full-context rollout.
